Every quotation is verbatim at its locator, and the resolver's facts check out against the git objects: the blob ids and line counts, the 29-line Q-6 block with one blank line removed, both exemplar mains on the old list, and USO/ roots only on the two no-deletion-fix branches. The operative part stands: change nothing in the exemplars now, and correct the scaffold first. Two clauses claim more than the quotations say.

**1. The default reading of "the same check" is the resolver's, not the owner's.** The resolution says to treat it as the same steps and list, "not byte identity, unless the owner says byte for byte". No quotation of the owner says that.
- The support offered is one record sentence (line 123) and an inference that "merge all three" ratified its meaning. Line 121 shows that word merged three pull requests; it did not rule on what "same" means.
- Texts on main lean the other way: the specification's "the one CI check" (line 281), and the field guide's "There is exactly one automated check, identical in every 7LM repository" (7lm@origin/main:L8/L6/7lm-field-guide.md:463, still live on main and on the beta).
- The owner's own word of 20 September 2026 is "mirror", which the resolver did not use (see the missed quotation).
- Practice is consistent on both lines of work: Auditonomous's file is byte-identical to the scaffold's on PR #28 and on its beta, and Autonomous keeps its block on PR #30 and on its beta. That is evidence of practice, not a ruling.
- So this should go to the owner as a question with both fixes written out, not be adopted as a default.

**2. The USO/ tolerance is framed as an open choice when the owner has already decided the substance.**
- The rename was carried out on the owner's word, "Lets do this today." (7lm@origin/main:L8/L6/history/harmonization-2026-09-04.md:168).
- The specification of record says "The root holds README.md, L7/, and L8/" (line 281) and lists "USO/ as the directory name of the interior | Renamed L8/" (line 996).
- Main's check therefore accepts a root its own specification calls not canonical. "Don't change the system unless you ask or are unsure" does not make that tolerance a design choice to preserve. It only means the correction is proposed, not applied unasked.
- The open question is when the scaffold's file is corrected: with the beta merge, or ahead of it as a change to the check alone.

**Smaller points.**
- "Don't adopt the beta until the owner merges it" is right, but its better ground is the missed quotation (scaffold first, the others mirror), not the beta record's "not a full-beta or release claim". That same record says the corrections followed "the owner's approval of R1–R6", so the candidate is not unapproved work; it is simply not on main.

- I found no later word of the owner that overrides the hold. "I didn't want anything automated yet" (17 October 2026) was said of another matter and does not withdraw the check, which the owner merged on 7 September and the specification names.
- A byte-identical Autonomous file would remove the only full copy of the retired Q-6 step. The command and the two reasons stand in the workflow comment alone; LEDGER.md:887 and .gitignore:52 carry fragments. The resolver's "enumerate first, then remove" condition is correct and necessary.

check.objection:
Every quotation is verbatim at its locator, but they support only half of the resolution.

**The pin holds, as an option and not a duty.** Naming the scaffold state is truthful and checkable. It needs one qualification the resolver did not make:
- The mirrored content last changed at bbb04dd (20 September 2026). The specification, the check (blob f43dd04) and the `L7/allications` and `L7/governance/controlled` sheets are the same blobs at bbb04dd and at c9dc061.
- c9dc061 became main at 18:08 UTC on 11 November; the mirror commit 8257118 is 18:33 UTC. No git object shows whether the pass read main at c9dc061 or at its parent 2e5a6d6.
- The spec line 837 cannot carry the pin as a specification rule; it is about a peer-owned definition, and the spec never calls the scaffold a peer.

**The "Declined" list does not hold.**
1. The guide's sentence is conditioned on "once the mechanism exists" and ends "None of this is built". The owner's own words put it "(in the future" and tie the list to "when you are n notified we pushed 7LM". The pass of 11 November was a hand mirror the owner ordered, not a push, so "as the guide asks" overstates.
2. Declining is a person's act: "A person decides, item by item, to follow or to edit." The owner declined nothing on 11 November. A session writing "Declined" over its own scoping choices attributes decisions to the owner that he did not make.
3. "Not changed" and "Left as found, for the owner" list the exemplar's own material left alone and defects found in it. They are not scaffold items refused, so relabelling them would misstate the record.
4. "Nothing" would be false at c9dc061. The scaffold there carries things neither exemplar has:
   - the owner's heading of 5 October in `L7/0.md` (2e5a6d6), absent from both exemplar `L7/0.md` files;
   - `L8/L6/in/` with the layer lists, which is all c9dc061 itself added;
   - sheet wording the sections themselves say was not taken ("the scaffold's sheets say things these sheets do not");
   - for autonomous, a check that differs from the scaffold's blob.
5. The record marks the owner's "list them in HOA" as "Read, not resolved." (line 358), and on draft PR #20 the guide that carries the rule is retired on the owner's word of 17 October. No precedent exists either: no earlier mirror section pins a commit or lists declines.

**A further owner word, not used, also points to "not yet".** "OUR 7Lm 0.md files will be absolutely complete and detailed and rigorous. My mistake. I want clear usage would start at a degree they choose, one day we can do choices for now everything is HOA" (/home/user/7lm@origin/main:L8/L6/history/harmonization-2026-09-04.md:376).

**Sequence.** The 11 November instruction asks only for the repositories to be updated "phsyciall; to match first". The addition is not part of that match and should not hold it up.

It stands unchanged on the PR #28 branch and on the auditonomous beta. On that reading, "match" can fairly be taken to cover live working files. This favours class (b) once the owner approves; it does not license applying it unasked.
